# HTTP API reference

Rimsky serves three HTTP surfaces.

- **The control API** answers 86 routes under `/v1`. It listens on port 8080 by default. Operators, the CLI, and client libraries drive rimsky through it.
- **The supervisor's async-callback listener** answers 4 routes. An external executor calls them to report an outcome, hold a dispatch open, or write attributes back mid-run.
- **The `sensor-webhook` ingress** answers 2 routes on port 9184. External systems post deliveries to it.

This reference gives every route's method, path, request shape, response shape, and auth posture.

## Control API conventions

### Versioning

Every control-API route sits under the literal path prefix `/v1`. The server serves that one prefix. `/v2/...`, `/v0/...`, `/api/v1/...`, and an unprefixed path all answer `404 page not found` as `text/plain` — the same answer a misspelled path gets, so a client cannot tell an unsupported version from a typo. There is no discovery route: `/`, `/v1`, `/version`, `/v1/version`, `/v1/versions`, and `/.well-known/versions` all 404, and no response header names a version. Ask the deployment's operator which release is running; the server will not tell you.

### Content type

The server answers `Content-Type: application/json` on every route except `GET /v1/ca-root`, which answers `application/x-pem-file`.

Requests that carry a body must set `Content-Type: application/json` on every route below `/v1` except `/v1/health`, `/v1/ca-root`, and the `/v1/observability/*` family. Any other content type answers `415` with an empty body. A request with no body skips the check.

### Authentication

Clients present an API key as `Authorization: Bearer <plaintext>`. The server hashes the presented string and matches it against the key ledger.

A deployment whose key ledger holds zero active keys runs in **anonymous mode**: a request with no `Authorization` header resolves to the anonymous identity, which holds every permission. Minting the first key ends anonymous mode immediately, and the same unauthenticated request then answers `401`. No configuration key or environment variable turns anonymous mode off — the mode is derived from the ledger, so the window stays open until a key exists. `GET /v1/auth/status` reports which mode a deployment is in, and revoking the last key answers `409` unless `?force_leave_anonymous=true` accompanies it.

Once keys exist, a missing header answers `401` with `{"error": "unauthorized", "denial_reason": "no_token"}`. Other denial reasons are `invalid_token`, `revoked_token`, and `expired_token`.

Three postures cover the routes:

| Posture | Meaning | Routes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| unauthenticated | No token consulted | `GET /v1/health`, `GET /v1/ca-root` |
| identity-only | Valid token required, no permission consulted | `GET /v1/auth/whoami` |
| permissioned | Valid token plus a grant naming the route's action | Every other route |

### Permissions

Each permissioned route names one **action**, a `noun:verb` string. A key's grant is a JSON array of entries:

```json
[{"action": "instance:read"}, {"action": "template:*", "mode": "dry_run"},
 {"action": "tag:set", "scope": {"template_tag": "release"}}]
```

A grant entry that does not match the route's action denies the request with `403` and `{"error": "permission denied"}`.

Wildcards accept exactly three shapes: `*`, `<noun>:*`, and `*:<verb>`. Any other shape — `instance:re*`, `*:re*`, `**`, `instance:read*` — is refused at key creation with `400` and a message naming the allowed shapes. The separator is part of the match, so `nod:*` does not reach `node:read`. The registry check skips wildcards, so a mistyped noun inside a valid shape (`instanc:*`, `banana:*`) mints successfully and then authorizes nothing, while the literal `banana:read` is refused `unknown action`.

**Scope narrows seven actions and no others.** `instance:create`, `template:register`, `template:deploy`, `template:undeploy`, `template:deregister`, `tag:set`, and `tag:delete` accept a scope; the other thirty-nine refuse one at key creation with `action "<name>" does not support scope`. There is one scope dimension, `template_tag`. No action accepts `instance_id` or `instance_key`, so a key cannot be pinned to one instance — a template tag is the only narrowing rimsky offers. The refusal comes at mint time and names the action, the rejected dimension, and the valid dimensions, so nobody ships a key believing it is scoped when it is not.

### Dry-run mode

Every permissioned route accepts `?dry_run=true`. The server validates the request, skips the mutation, and answers `200` with `{"dry_run": true, "<intent>": {...}}` — for example `would_have_created`, `would_have_deleted_instance`, `would_have_registered`. A value other than `true` or `false` answers `400` with `{"error": "invalid dry_run value", "dry_run": "<value>"}`.

A grant entry carrying `"mode": "dry_run"` forces dry-run on the actions it matches: the key cannot mutate through that entry even without the query parameter.

### Pagination

Eight collections share one contract: `?limit=` and `?cursor=`, an array plus a `next_cursor` string, and an empty `next_cursor` on the last page. They are `/v1/instances`, `/v1/templates`, `/v1/events`, `/v1/audit`, `/v1/tags`, `/v1/observability/instances`, `/v1/observability/events`, and `/v1/observability/templates`. The default limit is 100 on the core routes and 50 on the observability routes. The maximum is 500 on both.

The rest of the collections depart, and one paging helper will not cover them:

- `/v1/instances/{id}/frames` and `/v1/instances/{id}/messages` omit `next_cursor` entirely on the last page rather than sending an empty string.
- `/v1/instances/{id}/assets`, `/v1/instances/{idOrKey}/breakpoints`, and `/v1/claim-handles/{id}/holders` carry no cursor field at all.
- `/v1/instances/{idOrKey}/breakpoint-hits` pages on `since`, `next_since`, and `truncated` instead.
- `/v1/observability/executors` and `/v1/observability/claim-producers` carry no `next_cursor` and ignore `?limit=`.
- An empty page is `[]` on the core routes and `null` on the observability routes.

The cursor is not one token type. Core routes return an opaque base64 blob; `/v1/tags` returns the raw tag value. A malformed `?cursor=` answers `500` on `/v1/instances`, `/v1/templates`, `/v1/events`, `/v1/audit`, and `/v1/observability/instances`, with the internal decode error in the body — client input producing a 5xx, so retry-on-5xx logic will loop on a request that can never succeed. `/v1/tags` instead answers `200` and pages from the malformed value. A malformed `?limit=` diverges too: `/v1/instances` answers `200` and falls back to the default, `/v1/observability/events` answers `400`.

### Streaming

No control-API route streams or follows. `GET /v1/events` with `Accept: text/event-stream` answers `200 application/json` with a `Content-Length` matching a complete finite body, and so does `/v1/observability/events`. `?follow=`, `?stream=`, `?watch=`, and `?tail=` are accepted and silently ignored — the same envelope and the same row count as the parameterless call. `?since=` is a timestamp filter, not a resume offset. `/v1/instances/{idOrKey}/breakpoint-hits`, the one long-poll-shaped route, returns immediately. The CLI's `--follow` is client-side polling against these same finite reads; a client that wants a live view polls.

### Error shapes

Four different error envelopes come off `/v1`. Write the decoder for all four.

| Surface | Envelope |
| --- | --- |
| Core CRUD families | `{"error": "<human string>"}` — no machine-readable code |
| `/v1/observability/*` | `{"error": {"code": "not_found", "message": "..."}}` |
| `POST /v1/mcp` | JSON-RPC 2.0 error object |
| Unmatched path | `404 page not found` as `text/plain` |
| Wrong method | `405` with an empty body |

The flat envelope's extra fields come and go by status: a `401` adds `denial_reason`, a `403` does not, a `409` on undeploy adds `active_count`. One route can answer in two shapes — `GET /v1/observability/instances/{id}` sends the flat string envelope on `401` and the nested object envelope on `404`. The only machine-readable `code` anywhere is on the observability family.

Status codes hold for the common cases: a missing or invalid token answers `401`, an insufficient grant `403`, an unknown well-formed id `404`, and a conflicting write `409`. Two reads break the 404 rule and report an unknown id as an empty collection: `GET /v1/instances/{unknown}/messages` and `GET /v1/claim-handles/{unknown}/holders` both answer `200` with an empty list, so a client cannot tell "none" from "no such thing".

### Delete is not idempotent

No control-API `DELETE` is idempotent except `DELETE /v1/mcp`, which closes a session rather than removing a resource. A first delete succeeds and a second answers `404` with the resource's not-found string, on `/v1/tags/{tag}` (200 then 404), `/v1/instances/{id}/breakpoints/{id}` (204 then 404), `/v1/instances/{id}` (200 then 404), and `/v1/templates/{id}` (200 then 404). Deleting something that never existed answers `404` identically. The success code is not uniform either: `200` for a tag, an instance, and a template, `204` for a breakpoint.

A teardown script re-run after a partial failure therefore fails on every resource the first run removed, and distinguishing "already gone" from "delete failed" means parsing the message string. Teardown order is forced by the conflict rules: terminate instances, delete instances, undeploy templates, delete templates.

### Instance identifiers

An instance-scoped route spelled `{idOrKey}` accepts either the instance UUID or the instance key. One spelled `{id}` accepts the UUID only.

Eleven routes take the key: the instance read, delete, pause, resume, and terminate routes, the node listing, and the five breakpoint routes. Ten reject it: the five asset routes, the two frame routes, the two message routes, and the debug-override route. So an operator who names instances by key can create, inspect, pause, resume, terminate, and delete them by that name, but must first resolve the key to a UUID through `GET /v1/instances/{key}` to read frames, messages, or assets, or to issue a debug override.

The rejection is `400 invalid instance id`, which reads as "you sent a malformed id" rather than "this route does not take keys". The two spellings also disagree about an unknown name: `GET /v1/instances/never-created` answers `404 instance not found`, while `GET /v1/instances/never-created/frames` answers `400 invalid instance id`.

### Reserved prefixes

An instance key or tag beginning with `compose:` is reserved for the `rimsky compose` command. Creating one requires both the `X-Rimsky-Compose-Origin: 1` request header and the `compose:origin` action in the caller's grant; otherwise the request answers `400`.

## Health and bootstrap

### `GET /v1/health`

Unauthenticated liveness probe. Answers `200` while persistence is reachable and non-success when it is not. Persistence availability is the one dependency it checks.

```json
{"status": "ok",
 "supervisors": [{"id": "...", "concurrency": 4, "active_node_count": 1, "registered_at": "..."}],
 "node_counts": {"pending": 0, "fresh": 3, "stale": 0, "running": 1, "held": 0, "parked": 0, "failed": 0}}
```

The path is `/v1/health`, not `/health`. A probe written against `/health` gets a `404` from the control API.

### `GET /v1/ca-root`

Unauthenticated. Returns the deployment CA root certificate as `application/x-pem-file` with `Cache-Control: no-store`. A service needs this root to verify the control API's certificate before it can present a token to enroll, so requiring a token would be circular. The certificate is public; nothing secret is disclosed.

**This route exists only when the deployment configures service authentication with a CA.** On the zero-config default, and on an explicit `service_auth: none`, `GET /v1/ca-root` answers chi's `404 page not found` — unauthenticated, with an admin key, and with any key. The router has no such path; no handler is refusing the caller. Under `service_auth: mtls` the route appears and the control API itself serves HTTPS.

## Authentication and enrollment

### `POST /v1/auth/keys`

Action `auth:create`. Mints an API key and surfaces the plaintext exactly once.

Request:

```json
{"name": "ci-runner",
 "permissions": [{"action": "instance:read"}, {"action": "template:register"}],
 "expires_at": "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z"}
```

`name` is required. Each entry's `action` must be a known action or a legal wildcard shape; an unknown literal action answers `400 unknown action: <name>`. Scope dimensions are validated against the action.

Response `201`:

```json
{"id": "...", "name": "ci-runner", "plaintext": "rk_...",
 "permissions": [...], "created_at": "...", "expires_at": null}
```

**The plaintext is never retrievable again.** `GET /v1/auth/keys/{nameOrID}` and `GET /v1/auth/keys` return `id`, `name`, `permissions`, `created_at`, `created_by_key_id`, and `last_used_at`, and no query parameter changes that. An operator who loses a key recovers by rotating it, which mints a new plaintext under the same name and grant and revokes the old key id when the grace window passes; the name and the grant survive, the original secret does not.

Creating the deployment's *first* key with an `expires_at` answers `409`, because the expiry would return the deployment to anonymous mode when it lapses. Pass `?force_expiring_key=true` to confirm, or omit `expires_at`. A duplicate `name` answers `409 name already in use`.

### `GET /v1/auth/keys`

Action `auth:read`. Query parameters `name_filter` and `include_revoked=true`. Answers `{"keys": [...]}`. Not paginated.

### `GET /v1/auth/keys/{nameOrID}`

Action `auth:read`. `{nameOrID}` is a UUID or a key name. Answers the key record, or `404 no such key`.

### `DELETE /v1/auth/keys/{nameOrID}`

Action `auth:revoke`. Answers `200` with `{"id": ..., "name": ...}`, or `{"id": ..., "name": ..., "already_revoked": true}` when the key was already revoked. Revoking the last active key answers `409` with `{"error": "would leave zero active keys (anonymous mode); ...", "active_keys_after": 0}`; pass `?force_leave_anonymous=true` to confirm.

### `POST /v1/auth/keys/{nameOrID}/rotate`

Action `auth:rotate`. Body `{"grace": "1h"}` — a Go duration string, default 24h, must be positive. Mints a new key id and plaintext under the same name and permissions and sets the old key's revoke time to now plus the grace.

Response `200`:

```json
{"old_key_id": "...", "new_key_id": "...", "name": "ci-runner",
 "plaintext": "rk_...", "revoke_at": "..."}
```

Rotating a revoked key answers `409`, and so does rotating a key already in rotation grace. Rotating the deployment's only active key when it carries an expiry answers `409` unless `?force_expiring_key=true` accompanies it, because the new key inherits that expiry.

### `GET /v1/auth/status`

Action `auth:read`. Answers `{"mode": "anonymous"|"authenticated", "active_key_count": n, "admin_count": n}`.

### `GET /v1/auth/whoami`

Identity-only: a valid token is required and no permission is consulted. `auth:whoami` is not grantable — a permission here could only ask whether a key may learn its own name, and a denial would be unlearnable. Answers `{"kind": "api_key"|"anonymous", "key_name": "...", "key_id": "..."}`.

### `POST /v1/enroll`

Action `service:enroll`. Exchanges the caller's API key for a short-lived mTLS leaf certificate. Body `{"label": "..."}` is optional.

Response `200`:

```json
{"cert_pem": "...", "key_pem": "...", "ca_root_pem": "...", "not_after": "..."}
```

An unauthenticated caller is refused `403 enrollment requires an authenticated api-key principal`.

**Like `GET /v1/ca-root`, this route exists only when the deployment configures a CA.** Without one it answers `404 page not found` even to a key whose grant is exactly `service:enroll`, and the same stack answers every other route normally.

## Templates

### `POST /v1/templates`

Action `template:register`, scope dimension `template_tag`. Compiles, validates, and persists a template.

Request:

```json
{"spec": { ... }, "tag": "orders", "source": "orders.yml"}
```

Unknown top-level fields are rejected. `tag` must match `^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9._:@-]{0,254}$` and must not look like a content hash. Query parameter `?warnings_as_errors=true` promotes validation warnings to errors.

Response `201` on first registration, `200` on re-registration of the same canonical spec — registration is idempotent, and both answers carry the same `template_id`:

```json
{"template_id": "<content hash>", "tags": ["orders"],
 "validation_warnings": [{"path": "nodes[0]", "msg": "..."}]}
```

Validation failure answers `400` with `{"error": "template validation failed", "validation_errors": [...], "validation_warnings": [...]}`. Pointing an existing tag at a different template answers `403` unless the caller also holds `tag:set` on that tag.

### `POST /v1/templates/validate`

Action `template:validate`. Same body shape as register; persists nothing. Always answers `200`:

```json
{"ok": true, "validation_errors": [], "validation_warnings": []}
```

`ok` is false when errors exist, or when `?warnings_as_errors=true` and warnings exist.

### `GET /v1/templates`

Action `template:read`. Query parameters `state`, `limit`, `cursor`. Answers `{"templates": [{"id", "state", "registered_at", "source", "tags"}], "next_cursor": "..."}`.

### `GET /v1/templates/{id}`

Action `template:read`. `{id}` is a content hash or a tag. Answers the list item plus the full `spec`. Unknown id answers `404 template not found`.

### `DELETE /v1/templates/{id}`

Action `template:deregister`, scope dimension `template_tag`. Deletes the template and its tags. Answers `{"deleted": true}`.

When `{id}` is a tag and the template carries more than one tag, only that tag is removed and the answer is `{"deleted": true, "tag_only": true}`. A deployed template answers `409 template is in 'deployed' state; undeploy first`. A template with live instances answers `409` with `{"error": "template has active instances", "active_count": n}`.

### `POST /v1/templates/{id}/deploy`

Action `template:deploy`, scope dimension `template_tag`. Marks the template deployable, so instances may use it. Answers `{"state": "deployed"}`, or `{"state": "deployed", "no_op": true}` when it was already deployed — so the call is idempotent. A template in a non-deployable state answers `409`.

### `POST /v1/templates/{id}/undeploy`

Action `template:undeploy`, scope dimension `template_tag`. Rejects new instances of the template. Answers `{"state": "undeployed"}`, or adds `"no_op": true` when already undeployed. Refused `409` while any instance of the template is active, with `active_count` in the body.

## Tags

### `POST /v1/tags`

Action `tag:create`. Body `{"tag": "orders", "template": "<hash or tag>"}`. Answers `201` with `{"tag": ..., "template_id": ...}`.

**This route is not idempotent, unlike its siblings.** A second `POST` with the identical body answers `409 tag already exists`, and keeps answering `409`. Registering the same template twice and creating the same instance key twice both answer `200` the second time; creating the same tag twice does not. The idempotent form is a different verb, `PUT /v1/tags/{tag}`, which answers `200` twice — but `PUT` on an absent tag answers `404`, so neither verb alone is create-or-update. A re-runnable deployment script has to know which one to call.

### `GET /v1/tags`

Action `tag:read`. Query parameters `limit`, `cursor`. Answers `{"tags": [{"tag", "template_id", "updated_at"}], "next_cursor": "..."}`. The cursor here is the raw tag value, not an opaque token.

### `PUT /v1/tags/{tag}`

Action `tag:set`, scope dimension `template_tag`. Body `{"template": "<hash or tag>"}`. Moves an existing tag. Answers `200` with `{"tag": ..., "template_id": ...}`, or `404 tag not found`.

### `DELETE /v1/tags/{tag}`

Action `tag:delete`, scope dimension `template_tag`. Answers `{"deleted": true}` or `404 tag not found`.

## Instances

### `POST /v1/instances`

Action `instance:create`, scope dimension `template_tag`. Creates an instance from a deployed template.

Request:

```json
{"template": "orders",
 "instance_key": "nightly-2026-08-16",
 "params": {"region": "eu"},
 "attribute_overrides": {"by_node": {...}, "by_executor": {...}, "by_match": [...]},
 "paused": false,
 "service_bindings": {...},
 "message_queue_mode": "backlog",
 "target_daemon": "brave-otter"}
```

`template` is required and names a tag or a content hash. `message_queue_mode` is `backlog` or `coalesce`. `target_daemon` is required only in anonymous mode, where no key id exists to route host-daemon work by.

Response `201`:

```json
{"instance_id": "...", "template_hash": "...", "instance_key": "...", "node_count": 7}
```

Creation under an existing `instance_key` is idempotent: the same `instance_id` comes back with status `200`. A template that is not in `deployed` state answers `409`. Invalid attribute overrides answer `400`.

### `GET /v1/instances`

Action `instance:read`. Query parameters `template_hash`, `active` (`1|true|0|false`), `limit`, `cursor`. Answers `{"instances": [...], "next_cursor": "..."}`.

Each instance carries `id`, `template_hash`, `instance_key`, `params`, `attribute_overrides`, `attribute_overrides_match_counts`, `paused`, `created_at`, `terminated_at`, `service_bindings`, `created_by_api_key_id`, `target_routing_identity`, and `message_queue_mode`.

### `GET /v1/instances/{idOrKey}`

Action `instance:read`. Same object as the list item, plus `subscriptions` — one entry per publisher subscription with `id`, `publisher_name`, `kind`, `message_type`, `state`, `started_at`, and `failure_reason`.

Params named in the template's `params_redact` list come back as `"[REDACTED]"` here. See "Redaction is one surface" below for where the raw value still appears.

### `DELETE /v1/instances/{idOrKey}`

Action `instance:terminate`. **This deletes an already-terminal instance and its rows. It does not terminate a running one** — a running instance answers `409 instance is not in terminal state; wait for terminated_at to be set`. To force a running instance terminal, call `POST /v1/instances/{idOrKey}/terminate`, which is gated by `instance:kill`. The two verbs read the inverse of their names.

Answers `{"deleted": true}`. Deleting also releases committed durable claims, stops publisher subscriptions, and closes any run scope the instance still holds open, delivering a run-scope terminal for each. It discards nothing a subscriber has not taken: lifecycle deliveries already staged for the instance stay owed and drain after the row is gone.

The `terminated_at` field this route's own 409 tells you to wait for is not returned by `GET /v1/instances/{id}`. It appears on `GET /v1/observability/instances/{id}`, so the route that names the field and the route you would poll are on opposite sides of the permission line.

### `POST /v1/instances/{idOrKey}/pause`

Action `instance:pause`. Soft-pauses the instance; the supervisor stops claiming new dispatches for it. Answers `{"paused": true}`. An already-paused instance answers `409`.

### `POST /v1/instances/{idOrKey}/resume`

Action `instance:resume`. Answers `{"resumed": true}`. An instance that is not paused answers `409`.

### `POST /v1/instances/{idOrKey}/terminate`

Action `instance:kill`. Forces a running instance terminal: marks it terminated, fails every in-flight node-run, cancels pending messages, and ends open frames. Body `{"reason": "..."}` is optional. Answers `200` with the instance object. An already-terminal instance answers `200` unchanged.

## Nodes and runs

### `GET /v1/instances/{idOrKey}/nodes`

Action `node:read`. Query parameters `tag`, `limit`, `cursor`. Answers `{"nodes": [...], "next_cursor": "..."}`.

Each node carries `id`, `instance_id`, `node_type`, `executor`, `tags`, `cascade_mode`, `created_at`, `run_summary`, and `settling_signal_type`.

### `GET /v1/nodes/{id}`

Action `node:read`. `{id}` is a node UUID. Adds `latest_attributes` — the node's latest attribute bag — to the fields above. Unknown id answers `404 node not found`.

### `POST /v1/nodes/{id}/reset`

Action `node:reset`. Clears the failed-terminal settling-signal marker so the node becomes eligible again. It performs no state transition and does not re-dispatch. Answers `{"ok": true}` and records an `operator_override` event.

The route is narrow in three ways worth stating. It takes a **node** id, not an instance id — an instance id answers `404 node not found`. It refuses `409 reset only valid when node has a failed terminal run in some scope` when the node has no failed terminal run. And nothing else in the deployment moves: template, instance, and tag counts are unchanged. The `rimsky admin reset` CLI verb that fronts this route asks for no confirmation before calling it.

### `GET /v1/runs/{run_id}`

Action `run:read`. Reads one node-run's current lifecycle state, in flight or terminal.

```json
{"id": "...", "node_id": "...", "frame_id": "...", "state": "running",
 "terminal": false, "executor": "http-node", "enqueued_at": "...",
 "claimed_by": "...", "claimed_at": "...", "last_progress_at": "...", "async_ack_id": "..."}
```

Unknown id answers `404 run not found: <id>`.

## Messages

### `POST /v1/instances/{id}/messages`

Action `message:send`. `{id}` must be an instance UUID.

**An `Idempotency-Key` request header is required.** A request without one answers `400`. A retry with the same key replays the original send instead of double-sending, and answers `200` where the first send answered `201`.

Request:

```json
{"type": "order.placed", "payload": {...},
 "publisher_subscription_id": "..."}
```

Unknown top-level fields are rejected. `type` must be a message type the template declares, or the empty string — the empty type is the implicit root trigger every template accepts. An undeclared type answers `400` with `{"error": "unknown message type", "type": ..., "declared_types": [...], "implicit_types": [""]}`.

Setting `publisher_subscription_id` marks the send as a publisher send; the subscription must be live for this instance, or the request answers `403`.

Response `201` (or `200` on replay): `{"message_id": "..."}`. A terminated instance answers `409`.

### `GET /v1/instances/{id}/messages`

Action `message:read`. `{id}` must be a UUID. Query parameters `sender`, `type`, `sender_kind`, `frame_id`, `delivered_after` (RFC3339), `delivered_before` (RFC3339), `pending` (`true`|`false`), `limit`, `cursor`.

Answers `{"messages": [...]}`, with `next_cursor` present only when more pages exist. Each message carries `id`, `instance_id`, `type`, `sender`, `sender_kind`, `payload`, `received_at`, `delivered_at`, `frame_id`, and `cancelled`.

An unknown instance id answers `200` with an empty list, not `404`.

### `GET /v1/messages/{id}`

Action `message:read`. `{id}` is a message UUID. Answers one message object, or `404 message not found`.

## Frames

### `GET /v1/instances/{id}/frames`

Action `instance:list-frames`. `{id}` must be a UUID. Query parameters `state`, `triggering_message_id`, `limit` (default 50), `cursor`.

Answers `{"frames": [...]}`, with `next_cursor` present only when more pages exist. Each frame carries `frame_id`, `instance_id`, `state`, `triggering_message_id`, `root_run_scope_id`, `started_at`, `ended_at`, `last_progress_at`, and the triggering message's `message_type`, `message_sender`, and `message_sender_kind`.

### `GET /v1/instances/{id}/frames/{frame_id}`

Action `instance:read-frame`. Answers one frame joined with its triggering message envelope. A frame belonging to another instance answers `404 frame not found`.

## Assets

An asset is a committed durable claim against a claim producer that advertises the data-processing protocol. Its `{alias}` is spelled `{node_type}.{claim_alias}`; any other shape answers `400`. All five routes require an instance UUID.

### `GET /v1/instances/{id}/assets`

Action `asset:read`. Answers `{"assets": [...]}`. No pagination. Each asset carries `alias`, `claim_id`, `producer_name`, `scope`, `version_id`, `state`, `lifetime`, `claimed_at`, `holder_node_id`, and `node_type`.

### `GET /v1/instances/{id}/assets/{alias}`

Action `asset:read`. Answers one asset object, or `404 asset not found`.

### `GET /v1/instances/{id}/assets/{alias}/versions`

Action `asset:read`. Asks the producer for the asset's versions. Answers `{"versions": [{"version_id", "committed_at_unix_s", "producer_metadata"}]}`. A deployment with no data-processing registry answers `503`.

### `GET /v1/instances/{id}/assets/{alias}/materialization-history`

Action `asset:read`. Answers `{"materialization_history": [...]}` — the lineage records recorded against the asset's claim handle.

### `DELETE /v1/instances/{id}/assets/{alias}`

Action `asset:delete`. Releases the claim through its producer, then removes the claim-handle row. Answers `{"deleted": true}`.

Refused `409` with `active_count` while any holder of the claim is still active, and refused `409` when the producer cannot be resolved — rimsky will not orphan producer-side state.

## Breakpoints and the debug channel

### `POST /v1/instances/{idOrKey}/breakpoints`

Action `breakpoint:create`. Installs a runtime breakpoint.

Request:

```json
{"checkpoint": "before_dispatch",
 "matcher": {"node_type": "extract"},
 "signal_type": "terminal/error",
 "mode": "pause",
 "overflow_policy": "block_dispatch",
 "hit_ttl_seconds": 300,
 "ttl_seconds": 3600}
```

`checkpoint` is required and is `before_dispatch` or `after_terminal`. `mode` is `pause` (default) or `notify_only`. `overflow_policy` is `drop_oldest`, `block_dispatch`, or `auto_resume_after_ttl`; it defaults to `block_dispatch` under `pause` and `drop_oldest` under `notify_only`, and the two cross combinations are rejected `400`. `signal_type` is valid only on an `after_terminal` checkpoint. `hit_ttl_seconds` defaults to 300; both TTLs must be positive.

Response `201` returns the stored breakpoint, including `breakpoint_id`, `dropped_count`, `created_by_key`, `created_at`, and `expires_at`.

### `GET /v1/instances/{idOrKey}/breakpoints`

Action `breakpoint:read`. Answers `{"breakpoints": [...]}` — the unexpired breakpoints on the instance. No pagination.

### `GET /v1/instances/{idOrKey}/breakpoint-hits`

Action `breakpoint:read`. Query parameters `since` (a non-negative sequence number, default 0) and `limit` (default 100, maximum 500). Returns every hit after the cursor, not only unresumed ones.

```json
{"hits": [{"seq": 12, "hit_id": "...", "breakpoint_id": "...", "instance_id": "...",
           "checkpoint": "before_dispatch", "mode": "pause", "hit_at": "...",
           "node_run_id": "...", "frame_id": "..."}],
 "next_since": 12, "truncated": false}
```

Snapshot fields recorded at the hit are merged into each entry alongside these keys. This route returns immediately; it does not hold the connection open.

### `DELETE /v1/instances/{idOrKey}/breakpoints/{breakpoint_id}`

Action `breakpoint:delete`. Deletes the breakpoint and cascades to its hits. Answers `204` with no body. A second delete answers `404`.

### `POST /v1/instances/{idOrKey}/breakpoints/{breakpoint_id}/resume`

Action `breakpoint:resume`. Body `{"hit_id": "<uuid>", "overlay": {...}}`. `hit_id` is required and must belong to the named breakpoint. The optional overlay applies a one-shot attribute delta before the run continues.

Answers `{"resumed": true, "first_resume": true|false}`.

### `POST /v1/instances/{id}/debug/override`

Action `instance:debug-override`. `{id}` must be an instance UUID.

Request:

```json
{"action": "set_attribute", "node_type": "extract",
 "attribute_key": "retries", "attribute_value": 3}
```

`action` is `invalidate_node` or `set_attribute`. `node_type` is required for both; `attribute_key` is required for `set_attribute`.

The instance must be **paused or holding an unresumed pause-mode breakpoint hit**. Any other state answers `409` with `{"error": "instance not in debuggable state", "states": ["paused", "breakpoint"]}`. A `node_type` matching no node answers `400`. A node whose latest run belongs to a different frame than the active one answers `409` naming both frame ids.

Answers `{"ok": true, "gate_state": "paused"|"breakpoint", "runs_mutated": n}` and records a `debug.override.applied` event.

## Event and audit logs

### `GET /v1/events`

Action `event:read`. Query parameters `kind`, `instance_id`, `node_id`, `since` (RFC3339), `until` (RFC3339), `limit` (default 100), `cursor`.

```json
{"events": [{"id": 41, "instance_id": "...", "node_id": "...",
             "kind": "work_completed", "payload": {...}, "occurred_at": "..."}],
 "next_cursor": "..."}
```

`kind` is an **exact match, not a prefix**. `claim`, `subclaim`, `auth.`, `claim_`, and `claim*` are each rejected `400`, and the rejection prints the whole accepted vocabulary. The one prefix-shaped guess that does not error is worse: `claim/` parses as a signal type-path, answers `200`, and matches nothing, so it reads as an empty feed rather than a mistake.

### `GET /v1/audit`

Action `audit:read`. The same envelope under the key `audit`, restricted to the five `auth.*` kinds. Query parameters `kind`, `key_id`, `key_name`, `action`, `action_prefix`, `target`, `status` (integer), `mode`, `since`, `until`, `limit`, `cursor`. A non-`auth.*` kind answers `400 kind not in audit allowlist`.

Every gated request appends an `auth.access_attempted` row carrying the caller, the action, the response status, the mode, the protocol skin, and the request body as `payload.request_params`.

## Event kinds

`GET /v1/events` accepts 44 operational kinds plus three signal families. The rejection message on an unknown kind prints the whole list.

**Auth:** `auth.access_attempted`, `auth.access_denied`, `auth.key_created`, `auth.key_revoked`, `auth.key_rotated`.

**Node lifecycle:** `state_transition`, `work_started`, `work_completed`, `work_rejected`, `no_op_commit`, `operator_override`, `unresolved_executor`, `instance_terminated`, `error`.

**Named locks:** `lock_acquired`, `lock_released`, `lock_orphan_reaped`.

**Claims:** `claim_acquired`, `claim_held`, `claim_resolved`, `orphaned_claim_released`, `orphaned_claim_lost_race`, `claim_resolution.commit`, `claim_resolution.abandon`.

**Attributes and templates:** `attributes_substituted`, `attributes_committed`, `attributes_schema_failed`, `attribute_override_matched`, `template_resolution_failed`, `template_validation_failed`, `executor_schema_unavailable`.

**Debugging:** `breakpoint.hit`, `debug.override.applied`.

**Messages:** `message_sent`, `message_received`, `message.dead_lettered`.

**Child execution:** `fan_out_dispatched`, `fanout.children_created`, `subclaim.begin_candidate`, `subclaim.acquired`, `subgraph_internal_cascade_fired`, `subgraph.dispatched`, `subgraph.exit_carry`.

**Parking:** `parked_resume_started`.

**Service delivery:** `service_delivery.stalled`, `service_delivery.recovered` — one entry when a service's oldest pending outbox row first passes `service_delivery.stall_after`, one when that service next delivers. Both name the service and the outbox (`lifecycle` or `producer_verb`).

**Signal kinds** are any value containing `/`: `terminal/*`, `transient/*`, and `attribute/*/changed`.

Three properties of this vocabulary will surprise a client that assumes a regular scheme.

**The naming carries three separator conventions at once.** `claim_acquired` is snake_case, `subclaim.acquired` is dot-separated, and signal kinds are slash paths. One family is spelled both ways: `fan_out_dispatched` and `fanout.children_created` are both valid, while `fanout_children_created` and `fan_out.dispatched` are both rejected, and a single fan-out timeline carries both spellings side by side. Nine claim-related kinds start with three different first words — `claim_`, `subclaim.`, `orphaned_claim_` — so no lead token reaches them all. The one family that is consistent is `auth.`: every auth kind is dotted.

**Acquisition kinds do not have matching release kinds.** `lock_acquired` pairs with `lock_released`, and nothing else pairs. `subclaim.released`, `subclaim.resolved`, `claim_released`, and `claim_resolution.release` are each rejected as unknown; the claim side ends under `claim_resolution.commit` instead. `claim_acquired` and `claim_held` are both valid filter values and both return zero rows across a run in which a claim was acquired, held, and committed.

**Not every row carries both identifiers.** `work_started`, `work_completed`, `attributes_substituted`, and `terminal/success` carry both an instance id and a node id on every row. `instance_terminated` carries an instance id and no node id. The whole `auth.*` family carries neither. So narrowing the feed with `?node_id=` or `?instance_id=` silently drops the auth rows: the same filter that returns the node's `work_started` rows returns zero `auth.access_attempted` rows while the unfiltered query returns them, and nothing in the response says a kind was excluded rather than absent.

## Claim handles

### `GET /v1/claim-handles/{claim_handle_id}/holders`

Action `claim-holders:read`. Answers `{"holders": [{"id", "claim_handle_id", "holder_run_id", "state", "completed_at"}]}`. No pagination. An unknown claim-handle id answers `200` with an empty list.

## Lineage

All eight read routes share the action `lineage:read`. The three ancestor and descendant walks take `?depth=` — a positive integer, default 3, capped at 50.

### `GET /v1/lineage/runs/{run_id}`

The most recent lineage record for one node-run: `{"id", "record_kind", "instance_id", "frame_id", "observed_at", "record"}`. Unknown id answers `404 lineage record not found`.

### `GET /v1/lineage/runs/{run_id}/ancestors`

Answers `{"ancestors": [...], "depth": 3}` — the records the run's substitution references reach, walked upward.

### `GET /v1/lineage/runs/{run_id}/descendants`

Answers `{"descendants": [...], "depth": 3, "truncated": false}`. `truncated` reports that the scan budget was exhausted before the walk finished.

### `GET /v1/lineage/claims/{claim_handle_id}`

The most recent claim-terminal record for one claim handle. Unknown id answers `404 claim_terminal lineage record not found`.

### `GET /v1/lineage/claims/{claim_handle_id}/ancestors`

Answers `{"ancestors": [...], "depth": 3}`, walking parent claim handles.

### `GET /v1/lineage/claims/{claim_handle_id}/descendants`

Answers `{"descendants": [...], "depth": 3}`, walking sub-claim handles.

### `GET /v1/lineage/by-source/{source_type}/{source_id}`

Every leaf-run record whose substitution references name that source. Answers `{"records": [...], "truncated": false}`.

### `GET /v1/lineage/by-producer/{executor_name}`

Every claim-terminal record produced by that producer. Optional `?version=` narrows to one version id. Answers `{"records": [...], "truncated": false}`.

### `POST /v1/admin/lineage/prune`

Action `lineage:prune`. Body `{"before": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}` — required, RFC3339. Deletes lineage rows older than the cutoff. Answers `{"deleted": n, "before": "..."}`. Under `?dry_run=true` it counts instead of deleting.

## Diagnostics

### `GET /v1/admin/diagnostics/held-frames`

Action `diagnostics:read`. Frames held by a parked node-run. Held-claim holds are not reported here.

```json
{"frames": [{"frame_id": "...", "instance_id": "...", "node_ids": ["..."],
             "held_since": "...", "node_states": [{"node_id": "...", "state": "parked"}]}]}
```

### `GET /v1/admin/diagnostics/parked-nodes`

Action `parked-node:read`. The park roster: `{"parked_nodes": [{"instance_id", "node_id", "parked_at", "resume_at"}]}`. For the sender and receiver edges, read the wait-set route instead.

### `GET /v1/admin/diagnostics/wait-sets`

Action `waitset:read`. **Requires `?frame=<uuid>`**; a request without it answers `400 missing required ?frame= query param`. Optional `?receiver_run=<uuid>` narrows to one receiver.

```json
{"wait_set": [{"frame_id": "...", "receiver_run_id": "...", "sender_run_id": "...",
               "topic_kind": "...", "topic_filter": {...}}]}
```

### `GET /v1/admin/diagnostics/producer-outbox`

Action `diagnostics:read`. Undelivered producer-verb outbox entries.

```json
{"depth": 2, "oldest_enqueued_at": "...", "oldest_age_seconds": 41.2,
 "entries": [{"seq": 7, "producer_name": "...", "verb": "commit", "claim_handle_id": "...",
              "instance_id": "...", "attempt_count": 3, "next_attempt_at": "...",
              "last_error": "...", "enqueued_at": "..."}]}
```

### `GET /v1/admin/diagnostics/lifecycle-outbox`

Action `diagnostics:read`. What each lifecycle subscriber is still owed, one object per service with a pending row. `depth` counts every pending row for that service; `entries` carries the oldest 100. The staged payload is the subscriber's business and never appears here.

```json
{"services": [{"service": "...", "depth": 2, "oldest_staged_at": "...", "oldest_age_seconds": 540.0,
               "entries": [{"seq": 7, "scope_kind": "template", "scope_id": "...",
                            "event": "EventTemplateDeployed", "staged_at": "...", "age_seconds": 540.0,
                            "attempt_count": 3, "next_attempt_at": "...", "last_error": "..."}]}]}
```

## MCP

The three `/v1/mcp` routes carry an MCP JSON-RPC 2.0 skin over the same action set as the REST routes. All three take the action `mcp:read`; a `tools/call` is additionally gated by the per-tool action.

### `POST /v1/mcp`

The JSON-RPC dispatch surface. Methods: `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `resources/list`, `resources/read`. Any other method answers a JSON-RPC `method not found`.

`initialize` opens a session and returns the id in the `Mcp-Session-Id` response header. Every other method requires that header: a missing one answers `400` with code `session_required`, an unknown or expired one `404` with code `session_not_found`. Sessions idle out after 30 minutes.

`initialize` answers `serverInfo: {"name": "rimsky-control-api", "version": "v1"}` — the literal path prefix, not a release. The server supports exactly one protocol version, `2025-06-18`, and answers it for every request: an unrecognised `protocolVersion` falls back to that value rather than failing, so asking for `2024-11-05` and asking for `1999-01-01` both get the same answer.

A notification (a request with no `id`) answers `202` with no body.

Resources are breakpoint-hit feeds at `rimsky://instances/{instance_id}/breakpoint-hits` and `rimsky://breakpoints/{breakpoint_id}/hits`, both readable with `?since=` and `?limit=`.

### `GET /v1/mcp`

Opens the server-to-client SSE stream for an existing session. Requires `Mcp-Session-Id`. Answers `text/event-stream` and emits a keep-alive comment every 25 seconds. It carries no server-initiated messages at this release.

### `DELETE /v1/mcp`

Closes the session named by `Mcp-Session-Id`. Answers `200`. This is the one idempotent `DELETE` on the surface, because it tears down a session rather than a resource.

### Coverage

The tool catalog reaches every permission action the REST routes reach except `mcp:read` itself, and reaches nothing HTTP cannot. Two routes have no tool because they are ungated and the catalog is computed from the action registry: `GET /v1/health` and `GET /v1/auth/whoami`. An agent that needs to ask "is this deployment up" or "who am I" drops to HTTP for both. `observability_get` covers the whole `/v1/observability/*` family through one `path_suffix` argument.

The teardown tools carry the same name inversion as the routes: `instance_terminate` maps to `DELETE /v1/instances/{id}` (delete an already-terminal instance) and `instance_kill` maps to `POST /v1/instances/{id}/terminate` (force a running instance terminal).

## Observability

Every route below takes the single action `observability:read`. A key granted `instance:read` reads `/v1/instances` at `200` and is refused `403` on `/v1/observability/instances`.

### `GET /v1/observability/*`

The wildcard mount. Every path below `/v1/observability/` routes through it, and it is the surface the MCP `observability_get` tool addresses by `path_suffix`.

### The family is not a read-only mirror

Treat these as a second, differently shaped read surface, not a low-privilege copy of the primary routes.

- `GET /v1/instances/{id}` returns the instance at the top level; `GET /v1/observability/instances/{id}` returns `{"instance": ..., "cascade_graph": [...]}`, so a client reading `body["id"]` gets the id from one and nothing from the other.
- Nodes are addressed differently: the primary route takes a node id, the observability route takes an instance id plus a node type, and there is no by-node-id read on this side.
- The data differs. Observability instance rows carry `attribute_overrides` and `terminated_at`; observability template rows carry `spec`. The primary routes return none of those.
- Errors differ: the primary routes send `error` as a string, these send it as `{"code", "message"}`.
- Events are the one genuine pair — same envelope, same row keys either way.

### Routes

| Route | Query parameters | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /v1/observability/claim-producers` | — | `{"claim_producers": [service]}`, no cursor, ignores `limit` |
| `GET /v1/observability/claim-producers/{name}` | — | `{"service": ..., "pending_lifecycle_deliveries": [...]}`; unknown name `404` |
| `GET /v1/observability/executors` | — | `{"executors": [service]}`, no cursor, ignores `limit` |
| `GET /v1/observability/executors/{name}` | — | `{"service": ...}`; unknown name `404` |
| `GET /v1/observability/templates` | `state`, `tag`, `limit`, `cursor` | `{"templates": [...], "next_cursor": "..."}` |
| `GET /v1/observability/templates/{hash}` | — | `{"template": ..., "tags": [...]}` |
| `GET /v1/observability/instances` | `template_hash`, `active`, `limit`, `cursor` | `{"instances": [...], "next_cursor": "..."}` |
| `GET /v1/observability/instances/{id}` | — | `{"instance": ..., "cascade_graph": [...]}` |
| `GET /v1/observability/frames` | `instance_id`, `state`, `limit`, `cursor` | `{"frames": [...], "next_cursor": "..."}` |
| `GET /v1/observability/frames/{id}` | — | `{"frame": ...}` |
| `GET /v1/observability/nodes/{instance_id}/{node_type}` | — | `{"node", "run_summary", "events", "holdings", "latest_attributes"}` |
| `GET /v1/observability/node-runs` | `state` (`pending`\|`claimed`), `executor_name`, `instance_id`, `limit`, `cursor` | `{"node_runs": [...], "next_cursor": "..."}` |
| `GET /v1/observability/node-runs/{id}` | — | one flat run object with `claim_id`, `required_claim_producers`, `tags` |
| `GET /v1/observability/claim-handles` | `producer_name`, `holder_supervisor_id`, `node_type`, `holder_node_id`, `instance_id`, `limit`, `cursor` | `{"claim_handles": [...], "next_cursor": "..."}` |
| `GET /v1/observability/claim-handles/{id}` | — | `{"claim_handle": ..., "claim_holders": [...]}` |
| `GET /v1/observability/events` | `kind`, `kind_in` (comma-separated), `since`, `instance_id`, `node_id`, `limit`, `cursor` | `{"events": [...], "next_cursor": "..."}` |
| `GET /v1/observability/system/health` | — | `{"control_api_status", "database_status", "supervisors", "executors", "claim_producers"}` |
| `GET /v1/observability/system/summary` | — | counts: `node_runs_by_state`, `nodes_total`, `nodes_without_runs`, `node_runs_total`, `instances_active`, `instances_terminated`, `node_runs_claimed`, `node_runs_pending` |

The default limit here is 50 and the maximum is 500. `system/health` reports `database_status` by pinging the driver with a 2-second budget.

## Redaction is one surface

A template's `params_redact` list suppresses the named params on `GET /v1/instances/{id}` only, where the value comes back as `"[REDACTED]"`. The instance listing, the frame reads, the node reads, the instance-filtered event query, and the process logs are clean.

Five public reads return the value in full:

- `GET /v1/events` and `GET /v1/audit` — the carrier is the `auth.access_attempted` row whose `payload.request_params` holds the verbatim create request.
- `GET /v1/observability/events` — the same row.
- `GET /v1/observability/instances` and `GET /v1/observability/instances/{id}` — the instance's raw `params` object, sitting beside the redacted copy the ordinary instance read returns from the same deployment to the same key.

So the audit trail is what defeats the flag: recording the request that carried the secret is what publishes it. Anyone holding `event:read`, `audit:read`, or `observability:read` sees the raw value. Read `params_redact` as "hidden from the instance read", not as "kept out of the platform's records".

## Supervisor callback routes

The supervisor binds a separate HTTP listener for executor callbacks — port 8081 in the `rimsky-all-in-one` image. The base URL an executor should call arrives in its dispatch as `callback_url`; the supervisor stamps it from `callback.advertise_host` or a non-wildcard `callback.host`, and refuses to start with a wildcard bind and no advertise host.

Under `service_auth: mtls` this listener requires a client certificate from the deployment CA, and the callback route additionally requires that the presenting principal match the principal the dispatch was sent to.

### `POST ${callback_url}/v1/callback/{async_ack_id}`

Reports the terminal outcome of a dispatch the executor answered with `await_async`. The body is an `AsyncCallbackBody`: exactly one of `success`, `error`, or `park`.

```json
{"success": {"changed": true, "change_summary": "...",
             "attributes_delta": {...}, "tags": ["..."], "scratch": "<base64>"}}
```

```json
{"error": {"error_class": "upstream_timeout", "payload": {...},
           "attributes_delta": {...}, "tags": ["..."], "scratch": "<base64>"}}
```

```json
{"park": {"resume_at": "2026-08-16T12:00:00Z", "tags": ["..."], "scratch": "<base64>"}}
```

Zero outcomes or more than one answers `400`. A `park` without `resume_at`, or with a non-RFC3339 value, answers `400`. The legacy `{"type": "complete"|"blocked"|"errored"}` discriminator is gone and answers `400`. The top-level `events` field is reserved and must not be sent.

Unknown fields are ignored rather than rejected, so a body with a typo'd key parses as if the key were absent.

Response `200`:

```json
{"ack_status": "accepted", "current_dispatch_id": "..."}
```

`ack_status` is `accepted`, `rejected_run_terminal`, `rejected_run_stale`, `rejected_run_parked`, or `rejected_unknown`. On a rejection other than `rejected_unknown` the body names the canonical successor run in `current_dispatch_id`, so the executor knows which run superseded it. An unknown ack id answers `404 unknown_async_ack_id`.

### `POST ${callback_url}/v1/runs/{run_id}/keepalive`

Bumps the run's last-progress timestamp and renews the expiry on any claim the run holds, so a long dispatch is not reaped as orphaned.

**Requires the dispatch's `cancel_token` as `Authorization: Bearer`.** A missing or wrong token answers `401`. Answers `204` on success, `404 unknown_run_id` for a run the supervisor does not have, and `400 invalid run_id` for a malformed UUID.

### `POST ${callback_url}/v1/runs/{run_id}/attributes`

Writes attributes back mid-run and bumps the same progress timestamp.

Body `{"attributes_delta": {"progress": 0.4}}`. An empty or absent delta answers `400`. Requires the same `cancel_token` bearer authorization.

Answers `204` on success. A run that is not `running` or `held` answers `409` with `{"error": "run_not_active", "state": "<state>"}`. An unknown run answers `404 unknown_run_id`.

### `GET ${callback_url}/health`

Unauthenticated. Answers `200` with the body `ok`.

## Sensor-webhook ingress

The `sensor-webhook` service serves an HTTP ingress on port 9184 for external systems to post deliveries to.

### `POST /{path_prefix}/*`

Each live `webhook` publisher subscription binds one `path_prefix`. A request is matched to the subscription with the longest bound prefix that covers its path; a path under no bound prefix answers `404 no active sensor-webhook subscription for this path`. Two subscriptions cannot bind the same prefix.

Authentication comes from the subscription's `auth` block, which is required at subscribe time. Three modes:

- `none` — accept any caller.
- `secret_header` — compare the named header against the configured secret in constant time. A mismatch answers `401`.
- `hmac` — verify `<signature_header>` against `sha256=<hex>` of HMAC-SHA256 over `<timestamp>.<body>` with the configured secret, and reject a timestamp outside the replay window (300 seconds by default). A missing signature, a missing timestamp, a stale timestamp, or a mismatch answers `401`.

The body is capped at 1 MiB; a larger body answers `413`.

When the subscription names an `idempotency_header`, a delivery repeating the last-seen value of that header answers `200` and is dropped. The service otherwise builds an observation — `observed_at`, `path`, `method`, the decoded `body` (JSON when it parses, a string when it is valid UTF-8, `body_base64` otherwise), and `idempotency_key` when present — and posts it to the control API as a message on the subscribed instance.

Answers `200` on acceptance. A control API that cannot be reached answers `502 rimsky push failed`; a message the control API rejects is logged and dropped, and the delivery still answers `200`.

The `auth` block is honoured only by this publisher kind. The `http` poll publisher accepts the same block at registration, at deploy, and at subscribe, and then polls its upstream without those credentials and without a warning anywhere.

### `GET /health`

Unauthenticated. Answers `200` with an empty body.

## Health probes across the deployment

`GET /health` is not a shipped convention. Exactly two listeners answer it: the supervisor's callback listener (`200`, body `ok`) and the `sensor-webhook` ingress (`200`). The control API answers `404` at `/health` and `200` at `/v1/health`. One probe spec applied to every rimsky process will fail on the control API and on services that serve no HTTP at all.
